spec.name: Reversal v34
spec.notes: Mean reversion of recent returns across names.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.5, annual return 11%, maximum drawdown 5%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.53 to -3.60 (change -6.13). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 2.53 to 2.53. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 0.12 (as submitted, 5 bps: 2.53); it breaks even at 10.2 bps with daily turnover 0.80.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 2.53 against 2.53 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -2.09 against 2.53 in research, a gap of +4.62.
The best year gives 153% of total P&L (year 1) and calm regimes give -1112%; Sharpe is 1.0 in calm and 7.78 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.50 becomes 2.50 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 4.95 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.01, 95th percentile 1.02).
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The top 1% of days (5 days) give 516% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 650% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
